title: CHFA 2027 Round Two (federal 4% with accelerated and standard state credit) scoring, thresholds and state gap funds
status_note: Copied from the CHFA 2027-28 QAP Third Draft (posted September 11, 2026). CHFA's QAP page listed only the First, Second and Third Drafts on 2026-10-21; the plan is not adopted. Every figure here is labelled 'Not adopted' until it is. When CHFA adopts the plan, re-copy each line from the adopted PDF and set status to 'adopted'.

source.title: CHFA 2027-28 Qualified Allocation Plan, Third Draft
source.reading_note: The draft is a redline. Quotes below are the clean reading: struck text removed, inserted text kept, read from the rendered PDF pages, not machine text.

round.name: 2027 Round Two
round.credit: federal 4% (tax-exempt bonds) plus accelerated and paired standard state credit
round.quote: Round Two 2027: state credit Applications with federal 4 percent Housing Tax Credit ... Letter of Intent Deadline June 1, 2027, by 5:00pm MT ... Application Deadline August 2, 2027, by 5:00pm MT
round.dates_source: QAP Third Draft 3.B.2, read from the rendered page (the machine text runs struck and inserted digits together)

minimum_score.quote: Applications for state credit and federal 4 percent must meet a minimum of 115 points

primary_rule.quote: A proposed project must earn points in both of the primary selection criteria (low-income targeting and low-income use period) to be eligible for Housing Tax Credits in Colorado.

discretion.quote: Regardless of numerical ranking, the scoring does not operate to vest in an Applicant or project any right or reservation or allocation of Housing Tax Credits in any amount.

targeting.label: Low-income targeting
targeting.rule: Points = for each tier, (rent-restricted units at that tier / total rent-restricted units) x weight, summed. Units below 40% AMI count in the 40% row. Units above 60% AMI earn no targeting points. The table follows the minimum set-aside election: the 20-50 table has no 60% row, so 60% units earn no points under it.
targeting.quote: projects located in all counties will be allowed to use the weight factor of 50 for selecting the 60 percent AMI threshold, a weight factor of 72.5 for selecting the 50 percent AMI threshold, and a weight factor of 92.5 for selecting the 40 percent AMI threshold.
targeting.change_note: The Third Draft strikes the note that capped the 40% row at 60 percent of low-income units.

lowest_ami_bonus.label: Counties with lowest AMI
lowest_ami_bonus.quote: 20 additional points for counties with lowest AMI
lowest_ami_bonus.unconfirmed: The QAP does not list which counties qualify; CHFA names them in the application. Claim only with CHFA's list.

eli_targeting.label: Extremely low-income (30% AMI) targeting
eli_targeting.quote: Up to 10% of total units at or below 30% AMI 5 Points ... Up to 20% of total units at or below 30% AMI 10 Points ... Up to 30% of total units at or below 30% AMI 15 Points
eli_targeting.needs: a range of supportive services to the residents, at no cost to the residents
eli_targeting.unconfirmed: The Third Draft adds 'Up to' to each band. Read as 'at least' (the adopted 2025-26 wording), a share between bands earns the lower band; read as 'up to', it earns the next band. The page counts the lower reading and shows the other. Ask CHFA.

lines.label: Extended low-income use (15 or 25 years of extended use)
lines.quote: 15 Years of Compliance + 15 Years of Extended Use - 25 points ... 15 Years of Compliance + 25 Years of Extended Use - 40 points
lines.unconfirmed: Threshold #14 sets a 15-year minimum for federal 4% with or without state credit, but 5.A.2 asks 25 years for 'competitive state credit', and Round Two state credit is awarded competitively. Ask CHFA whether a Round Two application must elect 25 years.
lines.quote_minimum: Therefore, for federal 4 percent Housing Tax Credit with or without state credit, CHFA requires a minimum extended-use period of 15 years and for federal 9 percent Housing Tax Credit and competitive state credit an extended-use period of 25 years.

lines.label: Community revitalization plan (in a QCT)
lines.quote: CHFA will award one point for projects located in a qualified census tract that contribute to a Community Revitalization Plan

lines.label: Housing need (severe renter cost burden tier)
lines.quote: The percent of renter households severely cost burdened will be annually assessed and assigned into five tiers.
lines.unconfirmed: The QAP does not state the points for each tier; CHFA publishes the tiers with the application. Enter the points from CHFA's tier list.

lines.label: Community affordable housing priority
lines.quote: Three points may be earned for proposed projects to be located in a community that has an identified community affordable housing priority.

lines.label: Transit-oriented (TOC or TOD) site
lines.quote: Five points may be earned for proposed projects located at an existing or planned TOC or TOD site.

lines.label: Mixed income (no more than 80% tax credit units)
lines.quote: (Five points) Project that provides housing for mixed income (i.e., that have no more than 80 percent Tax Credit-eligible total units)

lines.label: Non-metro county of 180,000 or fewer people
lines.quote: (Five points) Projects located in non-metro counties that have a population of 180,000 or less.

lines.label: Rehab of blighted or historic buildings
lines.quote: (Five points) Rehabilitation of blighted buildings or locally or federally designated historic structures.

lines.label: Preservation
lines.quote: (Fifteen points) Preservation projects which are defined as existing Tax Credit projects in year 25 or later of their Extended Use period, or developments with project-based rental assistance or other operating subsidies guaranteed through a rental assistance contract (e.g. HUD Section 8, Rural Development Section 521, etc.) that is within three years of expiration

lines.label: No-smoking policy (whole property)
lines.quote: (One point) No-smoking policy, defined as projects that will institute a no-smoking policy for 100 percent of the project

lines.label: Modular or factory-built construction
lines.quote: (Five points) Projects maximizing construction efficiency by utilizing modular or factory-built construction.

lines.label: Universal design or Type A units (5%+ of units)
lines.quote: (Two points) Projects utilizing Universal Design or providing Type A units under technical accessibility standard options of either American National Standards Institute (ANSI) A117.1 or Uniform Federal Accessibility Standards (UFAS), which total at least five percent of the project's total units.

lines.label: Pet-inclusive
lines.quote: (One point) Projects that are pet-inclusive allowing one or more pet animals

lines.label: Nonprofit or Colorado housing authority as sole general partner
lines.quote: (Five points) Applicant is an approved 501(c)3 or 501(c) 4 tax-exempt organization, having an express purpose of fostering low-income housing, or a Colorado public housing authority; is the sole general partner

lines.label: Colorado housing authority as sole or majority co-general partner
lines.quote: (Seven points) Applicant is a Colorado public housing authority, will be a sole or majority interest co-general partner

lines.label: 25%+ of units for people experiencing homelessness or special populations
lines.quote: Fifteen points may be earned for the set-aside of at least 25 percent of the units for Persons experiencing Homelessness or Special Populations.

lines.label: Housing authority waitlist question on the rental application
lines.quote: One point may be earned by Applicants who commit to collecting information on their rental application about whether a resident applicant is on a housing authority waitlist.
lines.change_note: Down from two points, with a new requirement.

thresholds.label: Site control (deed, title commitment or executed agreement; an LOI is not site control)
thresholds.quote: Letters of Intent are not valid forms of site Control.

thresholds.label: Market study and Walk Score chart by a CHFA-approved, unaffiliated analyst; parking study if required
thresholds.quote: The Market Study must match the submitted Application regarding income targeting, unit mix, unit sizes, parking, and rents.

thresholds.label: Appraisal (acquisition/rehab only), no older than six months
thresholds.quote: The appraisal must be provided that is no older than six months from the date of Application.

thresholds.label: No outstanding noncompliance in Colorado; property management questionnaire
thresholds.quote: Applicants must submit the completed "Property Management Questionnaire" template

thresholds.label: Latest electronic spreadsheet application
thresholds.quote: Applicants must use the latest Application located on CHFA's website. Older versions will not be accepted.

thresholds.label: Readiness to proceed: zoning status letter, approvals and timeline
thresholds.quote: The Applicant must provide zoning status documentation from the planning department that includes parking requirements

thresholds.label: Phase I environmental (Phase II if RECs), no older than 12 months
thresholds.quote: Phase I or Phase II reports must be no older than 12 months from the date of the Application

thresholds.label: Third-party cost estimate on CHFA's cost summary template, CSI format; schematic drawings
thresholds.quote: Unaffiliated third-party cost estimates by an experienced cost estimator or general contractor that is entered on the CHFA Cost Summary template

thresholds.label: Team experience and track record certification
thresholds.quote: An Application not meeting the required experience will be rejected.

thresholds.label: Minimum amenities in all units
thresholds.quote: the amenity package for all units or building(s) will include the following minimum standards

thresholds.label: Green building certification (QAP Section 8)
thresholds.quote: the proposed project will receive a green building certification as described under Section 8 of the QAP.

thresholds.label: Narrative on CHFA's Word template, one-page executive summary first
thresholds.quote: The narrative must be submitted in Microsoft Word format and follow the document template available on CHFA's website.

thresholds.label: Extended-use election: at least 15 years for 4% (see the 25-year question under 5.A.2)
thresholds.quote: Federal 4 percent credit with or without state credit: A minimum election of 15 years extended use is required.

thresholds.label: Public hearing in the community (required: Round Two is a state credit round)
thresholds.quote: The Applicant must have conducted a Public Hearing in the community in which the proposed project is located

thresholds.label: Local government contribution, in writing (required: Round Two is a state credit round)
thresholds.quote: the Applicant must provide evidence that local government will provide some monetary, in-kind, or other contribution benefiting the proposed project.

thresholds.label: Existing tax credit project: year 10 or later of Extended Use (year 25 from the first credit year), a 50% new-construction expansion, or homeless or Special Populations housing
thresholds.quote: Applicants seeking new Housing Tax Credits for existing federal credit projects will not be eligible for the Competitive Housing Tax Credits unless the project is in year 10 or later of the Extended Use period (i.e. year 25 or later beginning with the first year of the credit period), except for projects serving Persons experiencing Homelessness or Special Populations or unless proposing a minimum of 50 percent expansion with newly constructed units.

credit_caps.quote: CHFA will accept Applications for a fixed amount of $1,000,000 in 2027 and $1,200,000 in 2028 of accelerated annual state credit and will pair up to $675,000 in 2027 and $600,000 in 2028 of standard annual state credit or TZ credit where eligible, for any one project or any one Applicant, or Affiliate of such Applicant, or Turn-key Project Developer of such Applicant in Round Two.
credit_caps.reading_note: Read from the rendered redline: '$1,10300,000' is $1,000,000 (the 1 and 3 struck, 0 inserted) and '$8600675,000' is $675,000.

without_pilot.quote: A fixed amount of $1,100,000 in 2027 and $1,300,000 in 2028 of accelerated State Credit and up to $800,000 in 2027 and $700,000 in 2028 of standard State Credit or TZ Credit, where eligible, to pair in Round Two.

underwriting.quote: Minimum 1.15 to 1.0 for all amortized debt throughout the initial 15-year pro forma period.

gap_pilot.quote_award: If state gap funding is requested at the time of Housing Tax Credit Application, and the project is awarded credits, a conditional award from either DOH or OEDIT will be offered.

doh.quote: DOH will pilot a commitment of $18 million for Round Two with a fixed loan or grant amount of $35,000 per unit and a maximum of $3.2 million per application.
doh.eligibility_quote: DOH cash flow loans or grants will be eligible for applications with an average area median income (AMI) midpoint of 48% or below for Round One and 52% or below for Round Two, or that are a Supportive Housing application.
doh.midpoint_quote: The AMI midpoint is the sum of the project's units multiplied by the AMI for each unit divided by the total units.
doh.terms_quote: DOH loans for for-profit applicants will have 2% interest and a term commensurate with senior debt in the application plus six months and will be a cash flow loan. DOH will provide grant funds to nonprofit or public housing authority applicants.
doh.unconfirmed: CHFA's October 1, 2026 webinar said 'Below' where the Third Draft says 'or below'. A deal within half a point of the line is flagged.

oedit.quote: OEDIT will pilot a commitment of $19 million for Round Two with a fixed loan amount of $30,000 per unit and a maximum of $2.6 million per application.
oedit.eligibility_quote: OEDIT funding will be Proposition 123 Concessionary Debt for applications that do not meet DOH gap funding eligibility described below, and are in a Proposition 123 eligible jurisdiction. Loans will have a 2.5% interest and a 40-year amortization schedule in either first or subordinate must-pay position.

doh_fallback.quote: If an application is outside of a Proposition 123 eligible jurisdiction and does not meet DOH gap funding eligibility described below, or if there are insufficient Proposition 123 gap funds, DOH will provide a loan with a 2.5% interest and 40-year amortization schedule in either first or subordinate must-pay position.
doh_fallback.unconfirmed: The draft does not say whether this fallback loan uses DOH's Round Two $35,000 per unit and $3.2 million cap. The page shows DOH's amounts and labels them unconfirmed.

thresholds_note: Threshold #18 (a non-CHFA bond issuer's inducement resolution and volume cap) is left out: the QAP exempts Round Two from it.

threshold_18_quote.quote: This threshold is exempted for Round Two Applications.

tie_out.note: Limits the application tie-out on the Submittal review page applies to the application's own figures.

credit_amount.section: 3.M.1, Calculation of Housing Tax Credit Amount
credit_amount.quote: The amount of Housing Tax Credits reserved will be based on the smallest of the amounts resulting from these calculation methods.

developer_fee.quote: Aggregate Developer Fee and Consultant Fee* Limits as a Percent of Certain Project Costs
developer_fee.base_quote: Certain project costs: Total cost to complete the project, minus the cost of land, developer fees, consultant fees, and project reserves.
developer_fee.acquisition_quote: Fifty percent of Acquisition cost (excluding projects serving Persons experiencing Homelessness or Special Populations)
developer_fee.tiers_text: Substantial Rehabilitation and New Construction: 51 units or more, 12%; 50 units or less, 15%.
developer_fee.boost_quote: An increase of the percent allowed, up to 5 percent, may be requested for projects serving Persons experiencing Homelessness or Special Populations with incomes at or below 30 percent AMI.
